profile.campus: Philadelphia metro, Pennsylvania (Flexential's Philadelphia-market data center, Collegeville)

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading:
Per Flexentials own individual facility page (tier-1 operator source, https://www.flexential.com/data-centers/pa/philadelphia/collegeville-data-center), this facility is located at 101 Troutman Road, Collegeville, PA 19426. The operator publishes a footprint of 203,703 square feet and 7.2 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building. Published certifications and compliance attestations include HITRUST CSF, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, NIST 800-53, ITAR, SSAE 18.

This Collegeville facility is Flexential's only current active Pennsylvania location; the company previously also operated a smaller Allentown building (formerly InetU's DC7 site, acquired via the ViaWest and Peak 10 lineage) that was vacated and is now being marketed for lease or sale by a third party, per Lehigh Valley trade press reporting documented elsewhere in this registry. Philadelphia's data center market remains smaller than the major East Coast hubs of Northern Virginia and the New York/New Jersey corridor, with growth concentrated more in suburban Philadelphia locations like Collegeville than in the urban core.

Pennsylvania's data center sales-tax exemption, established in 2016 as a refund capped at $5 million and restructured in 2021 into an uncapped exemption with reduced state tracking ability, is now projected by the Shapiro administration to cost $188 million in the 2026-27 fiscal year, rising to $517 million by fiscal year 2031, with total losses since inception potentially reaching about $2 billion by mid-2031, according to Spotlight PA's reporting. Cryptocurrency miners were banned from the program in 2024. State Rep. Greg Vitali introduced a bill to repeal the exemption, but acknowledged uncertain prospects given Governor Shapiro's public support for the program; Shapiro's own budget proposal assumes the exemption continues, with conditional added benefits for developers meeting environmental and employment standards.

reading.body:
Flexential Philadelphia - Collegeville has a published IT capacity of 7.2 MW, which represents the largest published capacity among the four facilities with disclosed figures in Pennsylvania and one third of the state's total of 22.2 MW. At an assumption of 40 kW per rack for AI training density, 7.2 MW translates roughly to 180 racks. The facility spans 203,703 square feet and sits in the Philadelphia metropolitan area, a regional market smaller than Northern Virginia or the New York/New Jersey corridor.

The site holds certifications for HITRUST CSF, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, NIST 800-53, ITAR, and SSAE 18, which qualify it for defense-classified work, financial services, and healthcare infrastructure. The certifications do not specify which customers are present or their workload types.

This is Flexential's only active Pennsylvania location after the company vacated its former Allentown building, consolidating the state to a single point of presence. Pennsylvania offers an uncapped sales tax exemption for data center equipment, projected to cost the state $517 million annually by fiscal year 2031, though the program excludes cryptocurrency miners and is subject to future legislative review. The campus's position as the state's leading published capacity facility reflects Pennsylvania's modest infrastructure footprint in AI compute relative to major East Coast markets.
